findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor AC2's leaf check to import statements, not raw substring presence — e.g. assert no line matching `^\s*(from|import)\s+.*\b(event_append|event_commit_git|event_prepare)\b` targets the sibling/parent, rather than mere absence of the string.
evidence: AC2: 'neither imports event_append nor the other, asserted by both module names being absent from their source'
Approach step 3: event_append 'points at the two new leaves'; step 1: event_prepare 'docstring points at staging.py' (docstrings reference module names in prose)
findings.finding: AC2's leaf-invariant proving method asserts leafness by 'both module names being absent from their source' — a raw substring check. Because the plan deliberately adds cross-referencing docstrings (event_append's docstring 'points at the two new leaves', and the leaves' docstrings point at neighbors), a prose/comment mention of 'event_append' (or the other leaf name) in a leaf's docstring would make this substring check FAIL even though no import exists, or conversely a substring match could be satisfied by a comment rather than a real import.
scenarios: A leaf file whose docstring mentions 'event_append' or the sibling leaf name trips the substring absence check despite being a genuine leaf (no import edge).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the substring-absence assertion with a grep anchored on import syntax: `! grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(from[[:space:]]+\S*\bevent_append\b|import[[:space:]]+\S*\bevent_append\b)' <leaf>` (and the other leaf name), so docstring cross-references do not trip it.
